summary: The note surveys upcoming photography and digital art festivals after September 1, 2023, presenting them as showcases of technology-driven creativity, from VR and AR to AI-composed art. It highlights specific festivals, artists and dates, and stresses their roles in mentoring emerging artists, celebrating diversity and offering education. It closes by urging readers to attend as a pilgrimage to the cutting edge of imagery.
one_line: A guide to fall 2023 through April 2024 photography and digital art festivals showcasing immersive tech, AI art, networking, diversity and education.
key_facts: Sofia Calderón presented work blending photography and digital manipulation at the Miami Lenscape Festival on September 15.
Jon Atkinson's cybernetic sculptures were shown at the San Francisco Pixel Parade on October 4, where interactivity is part of the art.
Emma Zhou's documentary exhibition 'Lives Unseen' premieres at the Seattle Insight Festival on November 12.
The Boston Virtual View runs December 5 through 10 and lets audiences wear VR headsets to explore a 360degree panorama of artistic worlds.
The Digital Horizons exhibition is slated for January 11, 2024, in New York City and features artificial intelligence that composes art.
The Atlanta Interconnect begins February 22, 2024, offering networking with photographer Lucas Reed (urban landscapes) and digital artist Elana Meyers (multimedia installations).
Cape Town's Kaleidovision opens March 19, 2024, showcasing work from underrepresented corners of the globe and indigenous art forms reinterpreted digitally.
The Denver Image Dialogue offers a week-long series of educational events starting April 6, including post-processing workshops and talks on ethical photography in times of social media.
Augmented reality installations at festivals let observers step into photographs themselves.
The note argues machines will augment rather than steal creativity, and that festivals nurture the next generation through discussion, mentorship and exposure.
